question: Where do I find the racks I scanned earlier? I can't find a History screen.
answer:
Past scans live on your Profile screen, not on a separate History screen.

1. Tap PROFILE in the bottom bar (the person icon, third tab).
2. Scroll to the "Recent Scans" section.
3. Tap any row to reopen that scan's results.

Only your 5 most recent scans are listed at first. If you have more, tap "Show all N scans" at the bottom of the section to reveal your full history ("Show less" collapses it again).

On a desktop or iPad, click "Profile" in the left sidebar — its subtitle is "Account & history".

If you saved an old /history bookmark, it still works: RackTrack now sends it straight to the Profile screen.

There is no History tab
/history just opens Profile
How do I see my previous scans
rootCause: The standalone /history route was replaced by a redirect to /profile; ProfilePage renders the 'Recent Scans' section fed by GET /api/scans. Bottom nav exposes HOME / SCAN / PROFILE only.

question: My Recent Scans list only shows 5 scans — where are the rest?
answer:
Nothing is missing. Recent Scans shows the 5 newest by default and hides the rest behind a button.

1. Open PROFILE and scroll down to the "Recent Scans" section.
2. Scroll to the bottom of the list.
3. Tap "Show all N scans" (N is your real total).
4. The full list appears; tap "Show less" to collapse it back to 5.

The button only appears once you have more than 5 scans, and only after the list has finished loading. There is no page-by-page paging — when expanded, every scan you are allowed to see is on screen at once, newest first.

Note that "allowed to see" depends on your role: a regular member sees only the racks they claimed, an org admin sees every rack in their organization's Sites, and the platform owner sees everything. So if a scan a colleague did is still missing after expanding, that is a permissions boundary, not a truncated list.
symptoms: Only 5 scans showing
Where is the rest of my history
Show all scans button
History list is cut off
rootCause: ProfilePage slices the /api/scans response to 5 unless showAllScans is toggled; the server route returns the complete list with no limit or offset parameter.

evidence.snippet:
// Show the 5 most recent by default; "Show all" reveals the full history.
const recent  = useMemo(() => (showAllScans ? scans : scans.slice(0, 5)), [scans, showAllScans]);

question: What do the numbers on each row of Recent Scans mean?
answer:
Each row on the Profile page's "Recent Scans" list summarises one scan:

• The picture on the left is the original photo taken of that rack. If no photo was kept, you get a terminal icon instead.
• The bold mono code (for example RK-4F2A9C1B — always "RK-" plus 8 characters) is the rack ID, the scan's permanent address. It is derived from the photo itself, so re-scanning the same image gives the same ID.
• The line under it reads "N dev · N units · N ports":
  – dev = how many devices RackTrack found in the rack.
  – units = how many rack units it mapped.
  – ports = how many port identifications have been recorded for that rack so far. This one grows every time you identify another port, so an older scan can show more ports than a newer one. A single one reads "1 port".
• On the right is how long ago the scan was taken — "just now", "12m ago", "5h ago", "3d ago", "2w ago", "4mo ago". If the scan has no timestamp you'll see a dash.

There is no search box and no sort control: the list is always newest scan first. Only the 5 most recent are shown; tap "Show all N scans" to see the rest.
symptoms: What does 3 dev 12 units 8 ports mean
Port count on history row keeps changing
Can I search my scan history
How is the history list sorted
rootCause: ProfilePage renders rackId, deviceCount, unitCount, portCount and a relative timestamp from /api/scans; portCount is the line count of port_identifications.jsonl, and the server sorts by timestamp descending. No search or sort UI exists.

question: How do I reopen a scan I did last week and get back to its results?
answer:
Tap it — that is all.

1. PROFILE tab → "Recent Scans".
2. Tap the row for the rack you want. Only the 5 most recent are listed; tap "Show all N scans" to reveal the rest of your history.
3. RackTrack reloads that scan and drops you on its results screen with the same tabs as when you first scanned it: Overview, Switches, Ports and Topology in the tab bar, with Network and Drift under "More".

The address it opens is /results/<rack ID> — rack IDs look like RK- followed by 8 characters, e.g. /results/RK-4F2A9C1B — so you can also bookmark or type that directly and land straight on the scan without going through Profile. Reopening a scan does not re-run the analysis and does not use your camera. If the rack no longer exists on the server, the deep link sends you back to the Scan screen and removes the stale entry from your local history.
symptoms: How do I open an old scan
Reopen previous result
Bookmark a scan
Get back to last week's rack
rootCause: openScan() fetches /api/scan/<rackId>/report?format=json and navigates to /results/<rackId> with the result preloaded in router state; the /results/:rackId route is deep-linkable and re-fetches via /api/scan/:rackId when opened cold.

question: I tapped an old scan and a red message appeared saying the scan was not found.
answer:
That scan's data is no longer on the server, so RackTrack cannot rebuild the results screen. The message is "Scan <rack ID> not found" and it appears as a red banner just under the Recent Scans heading on Profile — you stay on Profile, the app does not navigate anywhere.

What to do:
1. Stay on Profile and tap a different row in Recent Scans. If the others open, only that one rack's data is gone.
2. Take a fresh photo of that rack from the SCAN tab. You will get results again (a new rack ID if the photo is new).
3. If several old scans fail the same way, tell your organization admin — something removed rack folders on the server (specifically the scan's scan_meta.json).

Two related cases that look similar but are not the same thing:
- A rack that belongs to a different Site gives "Rack not found" (an access boundary), not "Scan ... not found".
- If you open a /results/<rack ID> link directly and the rack no longer exists, RackTrack shows no error at all: it quietly drops that entry from the app's local history and sends you to the Scan screen.
symptoms: Scan RK-... not found
Red banner on Profile when opening a scan
Old scan won't open
Tapping a history row does nothing / bounces to Scan
rootCause: buildScanReportData throws 'Scan <rackId> not found' when scan_meta.json is missing, and the report route converts any throw into a 404; ProfilePage surfaces the message in scansError. ResultsPage handles a cold-link 404 by pruning the local cache and redirecting to /scan.

question: My Recent Scans says "No scans yet." but I have definitely scanned racks.
answer:
"No scans yet." plus a "Start your first scan" button means the server returned an empty list for the account you are signed in as. Work through these in order:

1. Check who you are signed in as — your username and email are shown under your avatar at the top of the same Profile screen. A second account (or a re-signup) starts with an empty history.
2. Check whether you were moved to a different Site. Your history is the racks you claimed while in your current Site; if an admin moved you, the older scans stay with the old Site.
3. Remember that you only see scans you ran yourself. A colleague's scan of the same rack does not appear in your list.
4. If none of that fits, ask your organization admin — they can see every scan from every Site in the organization and can confirm the scan still exists.

A red error banner instead of "No scans yet." means the history failed to load, not that it is empty. The list is only fetched when the Profile screen opens, so navigate away and back to Profile (or reload the app) to retry it.
symptoms: No scans yet
History empty after signing in
Start your first scan button but I already scanned
My scans disappeared
rootCause: For a member, /api/scans intersects the outputs folders with tenantUserRackIds(tenant_id, user_id) — racks claimed in the CURRENT Site by THIS user. A different account, a Site move, or a colleague's claim all yield an empty set. The empty state renders only when there is no error.

question: I was moved to a different site and now my old scans are gone from Recent Scans.
answer:
That is expected. Your scan history follows the Site you are in, not just your login.

RackTrack records each scan as "this Site claimed this rack, and this person did it" (rack_owners: tenant_id + created_by). When an admin changes your Site, Recent Scans is rebuilt immediately from the racks claimed in your NEW Site, so scans you ran under the old Site stop showing for you. Nothing was deleted — the old records are still on the server under the old Site.

What to do:
1. Ask your organization admin to look the rack up — an org admin sees every scan from every Site in the organization, including your old ones.
2. If you know the rack ID (RK-…), you may still be able to open it directly for a while: rack access is checked against the Site baked into your login token, and that token is not refreshed when the admin moves you. Once you log out and back in (or the session expires), opening a rack from your old Site returns "Rack not found".
3. To get the rack into your new Site's history permanently, simply scan it again from your new Site.
symptoms: History emptied after being moved to another site
Scans vanished after admin changed my site
Rack not found after site change
Lost my history but colleague still sees it
rootCause: PATCH /api/orgs/:orgId/members/:memberId can set users.tenant_id. /api/scans for a member queries rack_owners by (tenant_id, created_by), and the :rackId guard denies members any rack their current tenant does not own — so a Site move detaches the member from previously claimed racks.

question: Do my past scans expire? How long can I go back and open one?
answer:
No — scans do not expire. Nothing in RackTrack deletes a scan because it got old. A scan you ran stays in Recent Scans and stays openable indefinitely: there is no 30-day, 90-day or 1-year cut-off, and no cap on how many scans you can have. (Recent Scans shows your latest 5 by default; tap "Show all N scans" to see the rest.)

Two things can make a scan drop off your list, and neither is a timer on your history:

• You are looking at it from a different place. As a technician you see the scans you yourself ran inside your current Site — not every scan the Site owns, and not scans you ran under a previous Site or a different account. The scan still exists; it just is not listed for you any more. (Site managers see their org's Sites; the platform owner sees everything.)

• The rack is no longer owned by any Site at all — for example after the organization or Site it belonged to was deleted on the server. Only then does the scan folder become a candidate for the server's orphan clean-up, and even then it is not immediate: the folder must also be older than the retention window (14 days by default), and the nightly job runs in report-only mode unless an operator has explicitly switched deletion on. An admin can also run it on demand.

Separately, live port drift history has its own retention (port events ~30 days, snapshots ~90 days, latest state per port always kept). That is the port timeline, not your scan — the scan, its unit map and its report stay put.

If an old scan matters for an audit, export it: open the scan and download the report (HTML, PDF, CSV or JSON). That gives you a copy that does not depend on the server at all.
symptoms: How long is scan history kept
Do scans get deleted after 30 days
Retention of past scans
Will my old racks disappear
rootCause: Nothing prunes scans by age while a rack_owners row exists; the only scheduled deletion is orphan GC, which targets outputs/RK-* folders with NO rack_owners row and is dry-run unless ORPHAN_GC_APPLY=1.

question: Can I put two past scans of the same rack side by side to see what changed?
answer:
There is no built-in "compare two scans" view — RackTrack has no scan-to-scan diff. Each scan stays reachable at its own URL, so compare them by opening both:

• On a laptop or desktop: open /results/<rack ID> for the first scan in one browser tab and the second rack ID in another tab, then flip between them. A rack ID opens cold — you don't need the original scan session.
• On the phone: open one from Profile → Recent Scans, note what you need, use Back, then open the other.

The side-by-side racks you may have seen are a different feature: they belong to a two-rack scan group ("Scan two racks"). On desktop, the Overview tab of such a group shows both racks of that group side by side; the other tabs (Ports, Network, Switches, Drift) and the phone show one rack at a time with a pill toggle, so live port probes don't run twice at once. Either way it compares the two racks of one scan group, not two scans taken at different times.

If what you actually want is what changed on a switch over time, use Port history & drift ("Continuous SSH telemetry") instead — it is built for before/after and has a Change log listing each recorded change.

Note: if a scan has been removed on the server, its /results/<rack ID> link 404s and sends you back to the scan screen.
symptoms: Compare two scans
Diff between old and new scan
Side by side past results
What changed since last scan
rootCause: No scan-to-scan diff exists. RackToggle only renders one rack of a multi-rack group at a time; each scan is addressable at /results/:rackId, so the practical workaround is two deep links. Temporal change is covered by the port history/drift view.

question: On a port's History tab, how far back does the "Value at" table and the change log go?
answer:
Open Port history & drift. The page targets your monitored switch automatically — there is no switch picker. Under "Interface inventory" tap a port tile, then in the panel that slides up tap the History tab (it reads "History · N" when that port has changes).

The History tab has two blocks:

• "Value at" — the port's state as it was 1h, 3h, 12h, 1d and 1w ago. Five fixed points, nothing longer than a week. Columns are Ago / Oper / Admin / Speed / Recorded. If consecutive points land on the same recorded state you get one row labelled "1h+" instead of repeated identical rows — that just means the port did not change across that span. (Snapshots are only written on change, so this is normal for a stable port.) On a port with no snapshots yet this block is hidden entirely.

• "Change log (N)" — the most recent changes for that port, newest first, capped at 200. N is how many are being shown, so N = 200 means you are seeing the newest 200 and older ones exist but are not displayed here.

The Timeline tab has its own Window picker: Last 1 Hour, Last 3 Hours, Last 12 Hours, Last 1 Day, Last 1 Week. One week is again the longest view.

If you need to prove a change older than a week, capture the evidence while it is still on screen.
symptoms: Port history only goes back a week
What does 1h+ mean in Value at
Change log cut off
Timeline window options
rootCause: The /history route computes exactly five offsets (1h/3h/12h/1d/1w) and requests eventsForPort with a limit of 200; the client's WINDOW_OPTIONS top out at 1 week and dedupedOffsets collapses identical snapshots into a '<first>+' row.

  { key: '12h', label: 'Last 12 Hours',sec: 12 * 3600 },
  { key: '1d',  label: 'Last 1 Day',   sec: 24 * 3600 },
  { key: '1w',  label: 'Last 1 Week',  sec: 7  * 24 * 3600 },
];

question: A port's change log says "No changes recorded yet." even though the port has been monitored for days.
answer:
That is a healthy port, not a broken history.

RackTrack only writes a history row when something about the port actually changes. The tracked fields are: operational state (link up/down), admin state, speed, duplex, flow control, active medium, description, and the three LLDP neighbour fields (chassis, port, system). Every poll is compared against the last stored snapshot; if nothing differs, neither a snapshot nor an event is written. A port that has stayed exactly the same since monitoring began therefore has nothing to log, so the History tab shows "Change log (0)" and "No changes recorded yet."

How to confirm the port really is being watched:
1. Switch to the port's Specs tab and look at "Last poll" — it should show a recent time. That timestamp is stamped on every successful poll of the device whether or not anything changed, so a recent value proves monitoring is alive.
2. "Last change" on the same tab tells you when the current state was first recorded — for a never-changed port that is effectively when monitoring began.
3. If you need to prove logging works, shut/no-shut or unplug/replug the port; the change appears on the next poll.

If "Last poll" is blank or very old, the problem is polling (SSH failure or backoff), not history.

One caveat for admins: description tracking can be switched off with the server env var PORT_DRIFT_TRACK_DESCR=0. If that is set, a changed port description will not produce a change-log entry.
symptoms: No changes recorded yet
Change log 0
Port history empty but port is monitored
Drift log shows nothing
rootCause: port_events rows are written only on a detected diff (writePollTxn compares against the previous snapshot), and snapshots are likewise written only on change — so a stable port legitimately has zero events.

question: Admin: how many scans does the Organizations console show me, and can I search or filter them?
answer:
The organization dashboard shows the 40 most recent scans across every Site in your organization, newest first — a fixed cap, not page 1 of N. (The platform owner sees no scan grid on the platform-level Organizations list at all — only the totals tiles, pending approvals and org cards; the owner gets the same 40-scan grid once they open a specific organization.)

Filtering is by click, not by typing — there is no search box:
• Click a person's card to narrow the grid to their scans; the heading changes to "Scans · by <username>".
• Click a Site row to narrow to that Site; the heading becomes "Scans · <site name>".
• Click "Show all", or the same card/row again, to clear the filter.

Because the filter is applied in the browser to the 40 rows already loaded, filtering by someone who has not scanned recently can legitimately show "No scans for this selection yet." even though they have older scans. To reach anything older than the last 40, open it by rack ID at /results/<rack ID>.

Note the Scans totals tile counts every scan ever claimed by your Sites, so it will normally be much larger than 40.

No scans for this selection yet but the user has scanned

Scan count doesn't match the grid
rootCause: GET /api/orgs/:orgId/dashboard returns recentScans with LIMIT 40 (owner dashboard LIMIT 15) while totals.scans is a COUNT(*) over rack_owners; OrgConsolePage filters that already-fetched array client-side by user id or site name.

question: Admin: if I remove a member, or the owner removes an organization, what happens to their scan history?
answer:
Two very different outcomes.

Removing a member (DELETE /api/orgs/:orgId/members/:memberId — server/auth.js:1331-1357):
• The scans survive. In one transaction rack_owners.created_by and invites.invited_by are set to NULL and only the user row is deleted (server/auth.js:1349-1352).
• The rack_owners rows keep their tenant_id, so the Site and the organization keep seeing the scans. In the console's scan grid the attribution falls back to "—" instead of "by <username>" (client/src/pages/OrgConsolePage.jsx:639).
• Caveat: a plain member's own history is scoped to racks where rack_owners.created_by = them (tenant.tenantUserRackIds, used at server/app.js:4917-4920), so once created_by is NULL those scans no longer appear in any member's personal history — only org admins and the platform owner still see them.
• Guardrails: you cannot remove yourself ("You cannot remove your own account"), an owner account, or — unless you are the platform owner — an org_admin. A site_manager can only remove plain members of their own Site.

Removing an organization (platform owner only, DELETE /api/orgs/:orgId — server/auth.js:1157-1191):
• For each Site in the org, every rack_owners and rack_groups row is deleted and audit_log rows have tenant_id nulled (server/auth.js:1164-1168); then invites, users, the Sites (tenants) and the organization row are deleted.
• The scan folders on disk are NOT deleted by that call — outputs/<rackId>/ simply becomes unowned. Org admins and members can no longer list or open them (canAccessRack / app.param('rackId'), server/app.js:193-225), but the RackTrack platform owner still can: canAccessRack returns true for role 'owner' and /api/scans leaves allowedRacks null for owner, so the owner still sees every folder on disk.
• Unowned folders older than 14 days then match the orphan sweep (server/lib/orphan_gc.js:53-56). That sweep is dry-run by default: the daily scheduled job only logs counts unless ORPHAN_GC_APPLY=1 (server/app.js:2143-2163), and POST /api/admin/orphan-gc/run defaults to dryRun=true. So files are not auto-deleted out of the box, but they are eligible.
• Export anything you need before deleting an organization; there is no in-app undo — only a platform owner can still reach the leftover folders.
symptoms: What happens to scans when I remove a user
Scans show by — instead of a name
Deleting an organization removes scan history
Can I recover scans after removing an org
rootCause: member.remove nulls rack_owners.created_by and deletes only the user; org.remove deletes rack_owners/rack_groups/users/tenants for the org, leaving outputs/<rackId>/ folders unreferenced and therefore orphan-GC eligible.

question: Internal: a scan is counted in the organization totals but never appears in Recent Scans — why?
answer:
Same diagnosis as the entry, with corrected anchors and two additions.

Accurate line references (the cited ones have drifted ~20-27 lines):
- server/app.js:4923-4928 — /api/scans: `fs.readdirSync(outputsDir).filter(name => name.startsWith('RK-')).map(rackId => { if (allowedRacks && !allowedRacks.has(rackId)) return null; const meta = readMeta(rackId); if (!meta) return null; ...`
- server/app.js:679-690 — readMeta: returns null if scan_meta.json is absent, and swallows a JSON.parse error to return null on a truncated/corrupt file.
- server/auth.js:1472 — org dashboard total: `SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM rack_owners WHERE tenant_id IN (${inList})`; server/auth.js:1443 — owner platform total: `SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM rack_owners`.
- server/app.js:3230-3234 — /api/select's comment explaining that it reconstructs and heals a missing meta instead of 404-ing.
- server/app.js:4933 and 4944 — the per-rack device_unit_map.json and port_identifications.jsonl reads that make the endpoint scale with the size of outputs/.

Two causes the entry omits:
1. rack_owners holds one row per (tenant_id, rack_id) claim, and a rack id is a hash of the source image — so if two Sites in the same org scan the same rack, the org total counts it twice while the history list shows it once. Duplicate claims alone can explain a totals/list gap with nothing wrong on disk.
2. Scope mismatch: for a member, /api/scans uses allowedRacks = tenant.tenantUserRackIds(tenantId, userId) (only racks THEY claimed), while the org dashboard total spans every Site in the org. A member's Profile list is expected to be smaller than the org total.

Also note the owner dashboard's own "Recent Scans" table (server/auth.js:1451-1459) is a pure SQL query over rack_owners joined to tenants/organizations/users — it will still show a rack whose files are missing. Only the Profile history list (/api/scans) and /api/racks are filesystem-driven and can silently drop it.

The diagnosis order is otherwise correct: check that outputs/<rackId>/ exists, check scan_meta.json is present and valid JSON, then compare against rack_owners rows for that rack_id.
symptoms: Scan count higher than the list
Rack counted but not listed
Scan missing from Profile but present in DB
Recent Scans slow to load
rootCause: /api/scans enumerates the filesystem and requires a readable scan_meta.json per rack, while dashboard totals COUNT(*) rack_owners rows; readMeta returns null on both missing and corrupt meta, so such racks are filtered out with no error.

      users: db.prepare('SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM users WHERE organization_id = ?').get(orgId).c,

question: Internal: a user says a "Clear" button wiped their scan history — where is that button?
answer:
It is not reachable. HistoryPage.jsx still exists and is still imported by App.jsx (line 18), but no <Route> renders it — App.jsx:312 makes /history a redirect: <Route path="/history" element={<Navigate to="/profile" replace />} />. Nobody can reach its "Scan history" header, its "Clear" button, or its "No past scans yet." empty state through the app. Treat any report about them as a stale build, a screenshot from an old version, or a URL typed by hand into a dev bundle.

What does still exist is the localStorage key rackTrackHistory:
- ResultsPage appends the current result to it and truncates with history.slice(0, 12) — so at most 12 entries, per browser/device, per WebView, never synced to the server.
- The only live readers/writers left are in ResultsPage: it writes on every new result (~line 1736) and prunes the entry when a cold /results/<rackId> link 404s (~line 1127).
- It is NOT cleared on sign-out. AuthContext logout() only drops the stored token and user keys, so rackTrackHistory persists across sign-out and across users on the same device. Only clearing site data (or the unreachable Clear button) removes it.
- It has no effect on Recent Scans, which ProfilePage serves entirely from GET /api/scans (server/app.js:4904, auth-scoped).

So: the authoritative history is server-side; rackTrackHistory is a vestigial, device-local 12-item cache. Clearing browser storage never deletes a scan.
symptoms: Clear button deleted my history
Scan history page with a Clear button
No past scans yet message
History differs between phone and laptop
rootCause: HistoryPage is dead code (imported, never routed); the local rackTrackHistory cache is capped at 12 entries and is device-local, while the real history comes from GET /api/scans.
